local_articles.title: Ukraine’s defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov resigns as part of reshuffle
local_articles.snippet: KYIV - Ukrainian Defence Minister Mykhailo Fedorov said on July 15 he was resigning as part of President Volodymyr Zelensky’s Cabinet reshuffle that saw the country’s prime minister step down. “It was a great honour to serve the Ukrainian people as defence minister,” he wrote on Telegram in a lengthy post listing the achievements of his ministry, which he had taken over in January. questions.background: The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) sets US monetary policy. Its policy announcements disclose members' votes and the policy preferences of dissenting voters.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : The Federal Reserve's official policy statement and voting record for the meeting concluding July 29, 2026, corroborated by contemporaneous news reporting. Resolution : Identify every voting member whose recorded position favors increasing the federal funds target range relative to the range immediately before the meeting. Include those members whether an increase is adopted or they dissent in favor of one. Accepted Answer Format : All qualifying members' surnames, listed alphabetically and separated by commas.
questions.current_reasoning: Major 2026-07-14 June CPI downside surprise and FOMC preview shift weight sharply from multi-member hike coalitions toward 1-2 regional-Fed hawkish dissents during a likely July 29 hold. June CPI fell -0.4% MoM (biggest drop since April 2020) and slowed to 3.5% YoY (vs. 3.8%-3.9% expected, down from 4.2% in May), while core CPI printed 0.0% MoM (unchanged vs. +0.2% consensus, easing to 2.6% YoY from 2.9%). Following the report—and despite Brent crude rebounding to ~$86-$87/bbl on renewed US-Iran Hormuz tensions and Chair Kevin Warsh telling the House Financial Services Committee today that the FOMC has 'no tolerance for persistently elevated inflation'—CME FedWatch July 29 hold odds surged from 58.3% on July 13 to 83.4%-87.7% on July 14 (hike odds ~12%-17%). July 8 June FOMC minutes showed a unanimous hold with 'a few participants' seeing a case to hike, and Continuum Economics' July 14 FOMC preview explicitly assesses that softer payrolls (+57k) and flat core CPI make a July hike unlikely, permanent Board governors are unlikely to dissent, and 'no more than two hawkish dissents are likely'—naming Cleveland's Beth Hammack and Dallas's Lorie Logan first, and Minneapolis's Neel Kashkari as less likely. Raising solo 'Hammack' (0.14 -> 0.19, #1) and 'Hammack, Logan' (0.14 -> 0.17), trimming the April trio 'Hammack, Kashkari, Logan' (0.11 -> 0.08), holding solo 'Logan' (0.05), and swapping 'Bowman, Hammack, Kashkari, Logan' out for 'Hammack, Kashkari' (0.03), leaving 48% outside the top 5 for unanimous hold, majority-hike coalitions, and other dissent sets.

questions.title: Which country will announce a new multinational maritime coalition to protect navigation through the Red Sea, Bab al-Mandeb Strait and Gulf of Aden by August 1, 2026?
questions.background: Attacks on commercial shipping since 2023 have heightened concerns about the security of maritime trade routes through the Red Sea.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official government announcements or contemporaneous reporting by reputable international news organizations. Resolution Conditions : Identify the country that announces the creation of a new multinational maritime coalition between July 1 and August 1, 2026, inclusive, with a stated purpose of protecting freedom of navigation through the Red Sea, Bab al-Mandeb Strait and Gulf of Aden. Joining an existing coalition does not qualify. Accepted Answer Format : The country's common English name.
questions.current_reasoning: Existing frameworks (US Operation Prosperity Guardian, CMF/CTF 153, IMSC/Sentinel, EU Operation ASPIDES, and the UK-France Hormuz coalition announced in April-May 2026) do not qualify, so a new multinational coalition specifically targeting the Red Sea, Bab al-Mandeb Strait, and Gulf of Aden must be announced in July 2026. Saudi Arabia (leader of the Red Sea Council and heavily reliant on its Yanbu Red Sea export bypass during the Hormuz closure) and Egypt (suffering massive Suez Canal losses, current CTF 153 commander, and alarmed by Red Sea/Somaliland tensions) are the top regional candidates to unveil an Arab/littoral maritime coalition. The United States (with Secretary Rubio touring the Gulf in late June on post-war security), the United Kingdom, and France (which has a Djibouti base at Bab al-Mandeb and co-led the Hormuz coalition) are the main Western contenders, leaving 31% tail mass on UAE, Turkey, China, Israel, India, or other states.

questions.background: Iran-aligned armed groups operate across several Middle Eastern countries, creating potential flashpoints for military confrontation with the United States.

A lot of oil is coming out, and the American companies are doing it.” Trump said there would be “a lot of deals” and announcements could be coming “this week or next week.” He didn’t share any details, just describing them as “massive, among the largest.” Securing such agreements would be a boost to al-Zaidi, who is eager to tap US investments to help raise Iraqi oil and gas capabilities.
